issues.failure_explanation: The operator $\Hcal = \Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}} + \K$ is a non-self-adjoint perturbation of $\Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}}$ because the integral operator $\K$ is not self-adjoint; its eigenvalues are generally complex, not real (as the authors themselves acknowledge in the proof of Lemma 2.6 where $\Im(\mu) \ne 0$). Furthermore, $\Hcal$ is bounded from below in real part ($\Re\langle \Hcal u, u\rangle \ge -C\|u\|^2$), so its spectrum cannot accumulate at $-\infty$; eigenvalues can only accumulate at $\infty$ with $\Re\lambda_n \to +\infty$. Finally, for non-self-adjoint operators, Jordan blocks can exist, in which case eigenfunctions of $\Hcal$ and $\Hcal^*$ cannot be chosen mutually biorthogonal with $\langle \varphi_n, \varphi_m^*\rangle = \delta_{nm}$. Downstream, Theorem 3.1 relies on this false biorthogonality and reality of eigenvalues to construct real-valued feedback shape functions $\alpha_j$ for each eigenvalue.

failure_location.quote:
Its spectrum consists of isolated real eigenvalues of finite multiplicity accumulating only at $\pm\infty$, i.e., $\sigma(\Hcal) = \{\lambda_n\}_{n \ge 1}$, $\lambda_n$ isolate, finite algebraic multiplicity, $|\lambda_n| \to \infty$.
    Furthermore, there exist (generalized) eigenfunctions $\{\varphi_n\}$ of $\Hcal$ and $\{\varphi_n^*\}$ of $\Hcal^*$ such that $\langle \varphi_n,\varphi_m^*\rangle = \delta_{nm}$, and the linear spans of $\{\varphi_n\}$ and $\{\varphi_n^*\}$ are both dense in $L^2(\Omega)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken Proposition 2.4 to state that $\Hcal$ has compact resolvent and purely discrete spectrum with finite algebraic multiplicity accumulating at $\infty$ with $\Re\lambda_n \to +\infty$. In Theorem 3.1, assume the unstable eigenvalues are semi-simple (or treat generalized eigenspaces) and adjust the feedback shape function construction by taking real and imaginary parts of complex conjugate eigenmodes to yield real-valued shape functions.
issues.overall_effect: The spectral description of $\Hcal$ in Proposition 2.4 is mathematically incorrect. Downstream, Theorem 3.1's proof of the Hautus test fails when eigenvalues with $\Re \lambda_j \ge -\delta$ are non-real (which produces complex eigenfunctions and thus complex control shape functions unless real/imaginary parts are taken) or when eigenvalues are defective.
issues.title: False assertions of real spectrum, bidirectional accumulation, and eigenfunction biorthogonality for non-self-adjoint Schrödinger operator
issues.why_classification: Correcting the spectral characterization and extending the Hautus control construction to handle complex conjugate and defective modes requires a self-contained nontrivial modification to Theorem 3.1, but avoids abandoning the overall feedback stabilization framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Next, taking $\lambda \in \rho(\Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}})$ and setting $\Hcal_{\mathrm{loc},\lambda} \coloneqq \lambda I - \Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}}$, one shows that the real-interpolation spaces satisfy

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (14) defines $\Hcal_\Pi = \Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}} + \K - \delta I + \hat\B \hat\B^* \hat\Pi$. Prior to Theorem 3.4, the authors define $\Hcal_{\mathrm{loc},\lambda} \coloneqq \lambda I - \Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Setting $A = \Hcal_{\mathrm{loc},\lambda}$ and $B = -(\delta I - \hat\B\hat\B^*\hat\Pi + \K)$ results in $A + B = -\Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}} - \K + (\lambda - \delta)I + \hat\B\hat\B^*\hat\Pi$, which has the opposite sign for $\Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and $\K$ compared to $\Hcal_\Pi$. Furthermore, since $-\Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}} \approx \sigma \Delta \le 0$, the spectrum of $A = \lambda I - \Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}}$ extends to $-\infty$, so $A$ cannot be sectorial with angle 0 (i.e. positive self-adjoint), and the associated Cauchy problem $\dot\psi + A\psi = \dots$ corresponds to an ill-posed backward parabolic equation.

issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem 3.4 as written constructs an ill-posed backward operator with mismatched signs instead of the forward parabolic operator $\Hcal_\Pi$.
issues.title: Sign error in operator splitting and definition of sectorial operator in maximal regularity proof
issues.why_classification: The error is a localized sign slip in the definition and splitting of the parabolic operator; replacing it with $A = \Hcal_{\mathrm{loc}} + \lambda_0 I$ immediately restores the valid application of maximal $L^2$-regularity without changing any theorem statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then $S \coloneqq T+K$ is closed also has a compact resolvent.

issues.failure_explanation: For a self-adjoint operator $T$, the spectrum is contained in $\mathbb{R}$. For any $\zeta = a+bi$ with $b > 0$, the distance from $\zeta$ to the spectrum is bounded below by $|\Im \zeta| = b$, giving $\|R(a+bi, T)\| \le 1/b$, not $1/a$. The proof states $\|R(a+bi, T)\| \le 1/a$, which is mathematically false (for $a>0$ small or when $a \in \sigma(T)$), and then sets the imaginary part $b = \|A\|+1$, which does not make the claimed bound $1/a$ small.

failure_location.quote:
By~\cite[Theorem V-3.16]{kato2013perturbation}, the self-adjointness of $T$ implies that $R(x,T)$ is defined for all $x \in \C / \R$ and 
    \[
    \|R(a+bi, T)\| \le \frac{1}{a}
    \]
    for all $b > 0$ and $a \in \R$, where $i$ is the imaginary number.
    By taking $\zeta = a + i(\|A\| + 1)$, we obtain the inequality~\eqref{eq:desired_inequality}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $1/a$ with $1/b$ (or $1/|\Im \zeta|$) in the resolvent norm estimate, which directly justifies that setting $\Im \zeta = \|A\|+1$ yields $\|A\| \|R(\zeta, T)\| \le \|A\|/(\|A\|+1) < 1$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma A.1 is invalid as written, though the conclusion that $T+A$ has compact resolvent is standard and true.
issues.title: Erroneous resolvent estimate and parameter confusion in proof of compact resolvent under bounded perturbation
issues.why_classification: The failure is a local variable/bound confusion between real and imaginary parts in a standard textbook proof; repairing it preserves the exact lemma statement with no downstream impact.
